sentences.text: Purpose.
sentences.say: Purpose.

sentences.text: Real problems have many inputs: a house has a size, rooms, floors and an age; an offer has an amount, a term and a credit score.
sentences.say: Real problems have many inputs: a house has a size, rooms, floors and an age; an offer has an amount, a term and a credit score.

sentences.text: This chapter extends the line to many features and shows how to compute with all of them at once, which is what makes machine learning fast enough to be useful.
sentences.say: This chapter extends the line to many features and shows how to compute with all of them at once, which is what makes machine learning fast enough to be useful.

sentences.text: Key ideas
sentences.say: Key ideas

sentences.text: With n features the model has one weight per feature and one bias: f(x) = w1 x1 + ... + wn xn + b = w . x + b.
sentences.say: With n features the model has one weight per feature and one bias: f(x) equals w1 x1 + ... + wn xn plus b equals w dot x plus b.

sentences.text: The dot product multiplies matching pairs and adds them up.
sentences.say: The dot product multiplies matching pairs and adds them up.

sentences.text: It is the core operation of machine learning.
sentences.say: It is the core operation of machine learning.

sentences.text: Vectorization means doing that arithmetic on whole arrays at once (NumPy).
sentences.say: Vectorization means doing that arithmetic on whole arrays at once (NumPy).

sentences.text: It is shorter and hundreds of times faster than a Python loop.
sentences.say: It is shorter and hundreds of times faster than a Python loop.

sentences.text: Gradient descent works the same as before, with one slope per weight.
sentences.say: Gradient descent works the same as before, with one slope per weight.

sentences.text: 7.1 The model with several features
sentences.say: 7.1 The model with several features

sentences.text: Ng's house now has four features: size x1, bedrooms x2, floors x3 and age x4.
sentences.say: Ng's house now has four features: size x1, bedrooms x2, floors x3 and age x4.

sentences.text: The notation: n is the number of features, x_j is feature j, and x^(i) is the list (vector) of all features of example i. The second house in his table is x^(2) = [1416, 3, 2, 40], and x^(2)_3 = 2 is its number of floors.
sentences.say: The notation: n is the number of features, x j is feature j, and x^(i) is the list (vector) of all features of example i. The second house in his table is x^(2) equals 1416, 3, 2, 40, and x^(2) 3 equals 2 is its number of floors.

sentences.text: The model gives each feature its own weight.
sentences.say: The model gives each feature its own weight.

sentences.text: Ng's example prices a house in thousands of dollars:
sentences.say: Ng's example prices a house in thousands of dollars:

sentences.text: b = 80: a base price of $80,000 before size, rooms and age.
sentences.say: b equals 80: a base price of $80,000 before size, rooms and age.

sentences.text: 0.1 on size: every extra square foot adds 0.1 thousand dollars, $100.
sentences.say: 0.1 on size: every extra square foot adds 0.1 thousand dollars, $100.

sentences.text: 4 on bedrooms, 10 on floors: +$4,000 per bedroom and +$10,000 per floor.
sentences.say: 4 on bedrooms, 10 on floors: +$4,000 per bedroom and +$10,000 per floor.

sentences.text: -2 on age: every year of age takes $2,000 off.
sentences.say: -2 on age: every year of age takes $2,000 off.

sentences.text: For the second house the model predicts 0.1 x 1416 + 4 x 3 + 10 x 2 - 2 x 40 + 80 = 173.6, so $173,600.
sentences.say: For the second house the model predicts 0.1 times 1416 plus 4 times 3 plus 10 times 2 minus 2 times 40 plus 80 equals 173.6, so $173,600.

sentences.text: Each weight says how much the prediction changes when that feature rises by one unit, with all the other features held fixed.
sentences.say: Each weight says how much the prediction changes when that feature rises by one unit, with all the other features held fixed.

sentences.say: 7.2 The dot product

sentences.text: Write all weights as a vector w and all features as a vector x. The dot product of two lists of the same length multiplies the matching pairs and adds the results, so the long formula collapses into one short one:
sentences.say: Write all weights as a vector w and all features as a vector x. The dot product of two lists of the same length multiplies the matching pairs and adds the results, so the long formula collapses into one short one:
Example: w equals 2, 3, x equals 10, 4, b equals 5.

sentences.text: The dot product is 2 x 10 + 3 x 4 = 32, and adding b gives 37.
sentences.say: The dot product is 2 times 10 plus 3 times 4 equals 32, and adding b gives 37.

sentences.text: This model, with several features and a straight-line combination of them, is called multiple linear regression.
sentences.say: This model, with several features and a straight-line combination of them, is called multiple linear regression.

sentences.text: 7.3 Vectorization
sentences.say: 7.3 Vectorization

sentences.text: In Python you can compute the prediction three ways.
sentences.say: In Python you can compute the prediction three ways.

sentences.text: NumPy counts from 0, so the first weight is w[0].
sentences.say: NumPy counts from 0, so the first weight is w0.

sentences.text: Writing every term by hand (w[0]*x[0] + w[1]*x[1] + ...) works for 3 features and is impossible for 100,000.
sentences.say: Writing every term by hand (w0*x0 plus w1*x1 + ...) works for 3 features and is impossible for 100,000.

sentences.text: The loop works but is slow. np.dot(w, x) is the vectorized form: one line, and far faster.
sentences.say: The loop works but is slow. np.dot(w, x) is the vectorized form: one line, and far faster.

sentences.text: Two benefits (Ng, video 22): the code is shorter and easier to read, and it runs much faster, because NumPy hands the work to compiled code and parallel hardware (the CPU's vector units, or a GPU) that multiplies all the pairs at the same time instead of one after another (video 23).
sentences.say: Two benefits (Ng, video 22): the code is shorter and easier to read, and it runs much faster, because NumPy hands the work to compiled code and parallel hardware (the CPU's vector units, or a GPU) that multiplies all the pairs at the same time instead of one after another (video 23).

sentences.text: On one run on my laptop, a million multiplications took 0.116 seconds in a Python loop and 0.00015 seconds with np.dot, about 750 times faster.
sentences.say: On one run on my laptop, a million multiplications took 0.116 seconds in a Python loop and 0.00015 seconds with np.dot, about 750 times faster.

sentences.text: The exact ratio changes from machine to machine; the gap does not.
sentences.say: The exact ratio changes from machine to machine; the gap does not.

sentences.text: The same trick updates all weights in gradient descent: instead of 16 separate lines, w = w - 0.1 * d updates all 16 at once.
sentences.say: The same trick updates all weights in gradient descent: instead of 16 separate lines, w equals w minus 0.1 * d updates all 16 at once.

sentences.text: With thousands of features and a large dataset, this is the difference between one minute and many hours.
sentences.say: With thousands of features and a large dataset, this is the difference between one minute and many hours.

sentences.say: R squared works the same way as before: it compares the errors around the fitted line with the errors around the mean.
